newsitem.title: USA: GM, UAW resume talks to end plant strike.
newsitem.headline: GM, UAW resume talks to end plant strike.

text.p: Bargainers for General Motors Corp and the United Auto Workers union resumed talks Friday morning in an effort to end a three-day-old strike by 2,800 workers at a powertrain parts plant.

A shortage of parts as a result of the strike has forced GM to suspend production at three car plants in Michigan -- in Lansing, Orion Township and Flint. Also, a car assembly complex in Oshawa, Ontario, that has two assembly lines was shut down Friday morning.
Negotiators talked all day Thursday, finally quitting at 0110 EDT/0510 this morning, said GM spokeswoman Darla Parks. They resumed bargaining at 0900 EDT/1300 GMT today.

Union members from Local 909 walked off the job at the Warren, Mich., GM Powertrain Group plant at midnight Tuesday. The plant makes four-speed automatic transmissions for front-wheel-drive vehicles, as well as wheels and suspension components.'

GM and the UAW are at odds over the automaker's desire to cut its workforce and buy more parts from contractors outside the company. The union is demanding that GM add more workers to ease overtime burdens and address health and safety issues.
